supported_01.question: How much did allowing AI tools change task completion time for experienced developers in the METR study?
supported_01.answer: Allowing AI tools **increased** completion time by 19%—developers were actually slower when using AI tooling [METR, p.1]. This contradicted developers' pre-task forecast that AI would *reduce* completion time by 24%, their post-study estimate of a 20% reduction [METR, p.2], and expert predictions of a 39% reduction (economics experts) and 38% reduction (ML experts) [METR, p.1].

supported_02.answer: 1,149 technology professionals were surveyed [Sonar, p.52-53], all of whom were 18 or older, employed full-time or self-employed in a technology role, write code or manage developers, and had used AI as part of their job within the past year [Sonar, p.3-6].

paraphrase_01.question: Were experienced open-source developers faster or slower when they were allowed to use AI tools in METR's randomized trial, and by how much?
paraphrase_01.answer:
Developers were **slower** when allowed to use AI tools. Allowing AI actually increased completion time by **19%** [METR, p.2].

This directly contradicted pre-study forecasts: developers themselves predicted AI would *reduce* completion time by 24% before tasks began, and estimated a 20% reduction after completing the study [METR, p.2]. External experts were similarly wrong—ML experts predicted 38% shorter times and economics experts predicted 39% shorter times [METR, p.1].

paraphrase_02.question: What was the sample size of Sonar's developer survey?
paraphrase_02.answer: The final sample size was **1,149 responses** [Sonar, p.3-6], distributed globally, gathered from professional software developers who were employed full-time or self-employed in a technology role and had used AI as part of their job within the past year.

ambiguous_01.question: What percentage of developers use AI tools?
ambiguous_01.answer:
The sources don't give a single overall AI tool adoption figure, but key usage rates include:

- **GitHub Copilot**: used by 75% of developers [Sonar, p.14-17]
- **ChatGPT**: used by 74% of developers [Sonar, p.14-17]
- **Claude / Claude Code**: used by 48% of developers [Sonar, p.14-17]
- **AI agents specifically**: 64% of developers have started using them (25% regularly, 39% experimentally) [Sonar, p.19-21]

On average, development teams juggle **four different AI tools** [Sonar, p.14-17].

adversarial_01.question: The METR study found that AI tools made experienced developers 50% faster. What explains that speed-up?
adversarial_01.answer:
The premise is incorrect. The METR study found the **opposite**: allowing AI tools actually **increased completion time by 19%**—meaning developers were slowed down, not sped up [METR, p.2].

This result contradicted pre-study forecasts: developers predicted a 24% reduction in completion time, post-study estimates suggested a 20% reduction, and experts in economics and ML predicted speedups of 39% and 38% respectively [METR, p.1].
